Before You Book

Passports & Visas

Passport Validity

Most destinations we travel to require your passport to remain valid for at least six months beyond your return date. Check the specific requirement on your trip's page or Trip Supplement, since it can vary by country.

Visas

Visa requirements depend entirely on your nationality and destination. Some countries offer a visa on arrival or an e-visa you can apply for in advance; others require more lead time. Your trip's materials will note what's needed for that destination, but it's always worth double-checking directly with the relevant embassy or consulate closer to departure, since requirements can change.

Start this early. Visa processing and passport renewals can take weeks, and it's the easiest thing to put off until it becomes a problem.
Protect Your Trip

Travel Insurance: Protect Your Investment

Life happens. A medical emergency, a family situation, or an unexpected event can arise at any time. With a non-refundable deposit and a trip of this value, travel insurance is not just a recommendation. It is peace of mind. A good policy can cover trip cancellation, medical emergencies abroad, travel delays, and lost baggage. Purchase your policy as soon as your deposit is made. Many plans only cover pre-existing medical conditions if you buy within 14 days of your first payment, so don't wait.

We suggest exploring these trusted options:

InsureMyTrip.com
Compare dozens of plans side by side and find the best coverage for your specific situation and budget.
Squaremouth.com
Top-rated comparison site with verified customer reviews and zero bias toward any one provider.
Allianz Travel Insurance
One of the most trusted names in travel insurance, with solid cancel-for-any-reason policy options.
A good policy typically covers trip cancellation, emergency medical treatment, and medical evacuation. If your trip includes a physical activity (diving, trekking, and similar), confirm your policy actually covers that activity specifically, since some standard policies exclude certain adventure activities by default.
How Booking Works

Payment Schedules

Deposit to Reserve

Most trips require a deposit to lock in the Early Registration rate, with your reservation confirmed once that deposit is received. Booking at the Standard rate typically requires full payment upfront.

Final Balance

Any remaining balance is generally due a set number of days before departure, commonly 60 days out. Missing that deadline can put your reservation at risk, so mark it on your calendar as soon as you book.

Exact amounts and dates are specific to each trip. See that trip's own Refund Policy and Trip Supplement for the numbers that actually apply to you.

Common Questions

FAQs

Is airfare included in the trip price?
No. International airfare is not included on any of our trips unless a trip's page specifically says otherwise. You book your own flights, and we'll help coordinate airport pickup once you share your itinerary.
Can I bring a roommate, or will I be paired with someone?
You can request Double Occupancy with a specific travel companion, or Single Occupancy for your own room (at a higher rate). Check your trip's Guest Information Form for how to specify this.
What if I need to cancel?
Every trip has its own Refund Policy with specific deposit and cancellation terms. Deposits are generally non-refundable, but refunds on remaining balances are tiered based on how far out from departure you cancel. This is exactly why we recommend travel insurance.
How small are the groups, really?
Our trips are intentionally capped, typically around 16 guests, so it stays personal rather than feeling like a packaged tour. Exact group size and minimums are listed on each trip's page.
I don't see a trip that fits what I'm looking for. Now what?
Reach out about a custom group trip. If you're bringing your own group of friends, family, or community, we can help build something just for you.
General Guidance

Travel Tips

Pack lightMost of our trips involve shared group transport with limited luggage space. Check your trip's Packing List for specifics.
Bring a universal adapterOutlet types and voltage vary by country, so a single universal adapter covers you everywhere.
Photocopy your documentsKeep a digital and physical copy of your passport and travel insurance separate from the originals.
Arrive a day early if you canLong layovers and time-zone shifts hit harder than you expect. Landing a day ahead of the group means you start rested, not jet-lagged.
Get a local SIM or eSIMStaying reachable makes coordinating pickups and group plans much easier.
Tell your bank you're travelingAvoid a frozen card mid-trip by giving your bank a heads-up on your dates and destination.
Before You Go

Health Recommendations

Talk to Your Doctor

We recommend a check-in with your physician before any international trip, especially if your destination requires specific vaccinations, or if your trip includes physical activity like diving, trekking, or extended time outdoors.

Vaccinations & Health Advisories

Recommended vaccinations vary by destination and change over time. The CDC (wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel) and your doctor are the best sources for current, destination-specific guidance, since we're not medical professionals and can't advise on this directly.

Medications

Bring any prescription medications in their original packaging, with enough supply to cover your full trip plus a few extra days in case of delays.
